bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷七十 東漢世家第十: 劉旻
title.en: Volume 70: Hereditary House of Eastern Han
title.raw: 卷七十 東漢世家第十: 劉旻 Volume 70: Hereditary House of Eastern Han

sentences.zh: 劉旻，漢高祖母弟也。

translations.literal: Liu Min was the uterine younger brother of Emperor Gaozu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min was the full younger brother of Later Han's founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 初名崇，為人美須髯，目重瞳子。

translations.literal: His original name was Chong; he was a man of handsome beard and mustache, with double pupils in his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Born Chong, he was strikingly handsome, with a fine beard and mustache and double pupils.

sentences.zh: 少無賴，嗜酒好博，嘗黥為卒。

translations.literal: In his youth he was a scoundrel, addicted to wine and fond of gambling, and was once tattooed and made a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was unruly and dissolute, given to drink and dice, and at one point was branded and pressed into the ranks.

sentences.zh: 高祖事晉為河東節度使，以旻為都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu served Jin as military governor of Hedong, he appointed Min commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still in Jin's service as governor of Hedong, he made Min his chief commander.

sentences.zh: 高祖即帝位，以為太原尹、北京留守、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Min was made governor of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, and Palace Attendant with joint authority as Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Min was appointed prefect of Taiyuan, defender of the northern capital, and concurrent Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 隱帝時，累加中書令。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yin, he was repeatedly promoted until he reached Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the youthful Yin Emperor, he was promoted repeatedly until he held the post of Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 隱帝少，政在大臣，周太祖為樞密使，新討三叛，立大功，而與旻素有隙，旻頗不自安，謂判官鄭珙曰：「主上幼弱，政在權臣，而吾與郭公不葉，時事如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor was young and power lay with the ministers. Zhou Taizu was Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he had just suppressed the Three Rebellions and won great merit, yet he and Min had long been at odds. Min felt quite ill at ease. He said to his aide Zheng Qing: "The sovereign is young and weak, and government rests with powerful ministers. Guo and I do not get on—what is to become of things?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin was still a child, so state affairs were in the hands of the senior ministers. Guo Wei, lately appointed chief of the privy council, had just crushed the three major rebellions and won towering credit—yet he and Min had old grievances. Min grew increasingly uneasy and asked his staff officer Zheng Qing, "The Son of Heaven is young, and power sits with the men at court. Guo and I have never been on good terms—how do you read the situation?

sentences.zh: 珙曰：「漢政將亂矣！

translations.literal: Qing said: "The rule of Han is about to fall into chaos!
translations.idiomatic: Qing replied, "The Han regime is heading for chaos!

sentences.zh: 晉陽兵雄天下，而地形險固，十州征賦足以自給。

translations.literal: The troops of Jinyang are the strongest under Heaven, and the terrain there is precipitous and secure; the revenues of ten prefectures are enough to sustain you on your own.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang commands the finest soldiers in the realm, and its mountains make it a natural fortress. Taxes from ten prefectures would be enough to keep you supplied.

sentences.zh: 公為宗室，不以此時為計，後必為人所制。」

translations.literal: You are of the imperial clan; if you do not take thought for yourself at this moment, you will later be controlled by others."
translations.idiomatic: You are a kinsman of the house—if you fail to act now, others will certainly hem you in later.

sentences.zh: 旻曰：「子言，乃吾意也。」

translations.literal: Min said: "Your words are exactly my own thought."
translations.idiomatic: Min said, "That is precisely what I mean.

sentences.zh: 乃罷上供征賦，收豪傑，籍丁民以益兵。

translations.literal: He then stopped forwarding tax levies to the central court, gathered bold spirits, and registered male commoners to increase his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped sending tribute levies up to the capital, recruited bold spirits, and registered civilian males to swell his army.

sentences.zh: 三年，周太祖起魏，隱帝遇弒，旻乃謀舉兵。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zhou Taizu rose in Wei; Emperor Yin was murdered; Min then plotted to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Guo Wei rebelled in Wei; the young emperor was assassinated; Min now planned to take the field.

sentences.zh: 周太祖之自魏入也，反狀已白，而漢大臣不即推尊之，故未敢即立，乃白漢太后，立旻子赟為漢嗣，遣宰相馮道迎赟於徐州。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu marched from Wei toward the capital, his rebellion was already exposed, yet the Han ministers did not immediately acclaim him, so he did not dare to take the throne at once. He informed the Han empress dowager, installed Min's son Yun as heir to Han, and sent Grand Councillor Feng Dao to welcome Yun from Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo marched out of Wei toward Luoyang, his treason was plain, but the Han court still would not proclaim him emperor, so he hesitated to take the throne outright. He had the empress dowager name Yun, Min's son, as heir and sent Feng Dao to fetch him from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，人皆知太祖之非實意也，旻獨喜曰：「吾兒為帝矣，何患！」

translations.literal: At that time everyone knew the Taizu had no genuine intention, but Min alone rejoiced and said: "My son has become emperor—what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: All who watched knew Guo's pledge was hollow, yet Min alone rejoiced: "My son is emperor—what danger remains?

sentences.zh: 乃罷兵，遣人至京師。

translations.literal: He then disbanded his troops and sent someone to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He stood down his army and sent envoys to the capital.

sentences.zh: 周太祖少賤，黥其頸上為飛雀，世謂之郭雀兒。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu had been low-born in his youth; he was tattooed on the neck with a flying sparrow, and the world called him Guo the Sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei had begun life in the lowest ranks; a tattoo of a flying sparrow on his neck earned him the nickname Sparrow Guo.

sentences.zh: 太祖見旻使者，具道所以立赟之意，因自指其頸以示使者曰：「自古豈有雕青天子？

translations.literal: The Taizu received Min's envoy, fully explained his reasons for enthroning Yun, and, pointing to his own neck, showed the envoy and said: "Since antiquity has there ever been a tattooed Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Min's messenger, he laid out at length why Yun should reign and, tapping his tattooed neck, asked, "When in history has a Son of Heaven borne a convict's mark?

sentences.zh: 幸公無以我為疑。」

translations.literal: May you, sir, not doubt me on that account."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you not to doubt me for this.

sentences.zh: 旻喜，益信以為然。

translations.literal: Min was delighted and believed it all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Min was overjoyed and believed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 太原少尹李驤曰：「郭公舉兵犯順，其勢不能為漢臣，必不為劉氏立後。」

translations.literal: Li Xiang, vice-prefect of Taiyuan, said: "Lord Guo has raised troops in violation of the throne; in his position he cannot remain a subject of Han and will certainly not establish a successor for the Liu house."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang, deputy governor of Taiyuan, warned, "Guo has taken up arms against his sovereign; he cannot remain Han's minister and will never install a Liu heir.

sentences.zh: 因勸旻以兵下太行，控孟津以俟變，庶幾赟得立，赟立而罷兵可也。

translations.literal: He therefore urged Min to lead troops down the Taihang range, seize Meng Ford to await developments, so that perhaps Yun might be enthroned; once Yun was enthroned, standing down the army would be possible.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Min to march through the Taihang passes, hold Meng Ford, and wait on events—perhaps Yun could still be seated; once Yun reigned, they could disband.

sentences.zh: 旻大罵曰：「驤腐儒，欲離間我父子！」

translations.literal: Min cursed loudly: "Xiang, you rotten Confucian—trying to drive a wedge between father and son!"
translations.idiomatic: Min roared, "You pedant—trying to set my son and me at odds!

sentences.zh: 命左右牽出斬之。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to drag him out and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He had attendants haul Xiang out and behead him.

sentences.zh: 驤臨刑嘆曰：「吾為愚人畫計，死誠宜矣！

translations.literal: At the block Xiang sighed and said: "I drew up plans for a fool—death is indeed fitting!
translations.idiomatic: On the scaffold Xiang sighed, "I schemed for a fool—death is only fair.

sentences.zh: 然吾妻病，不可獨存，願與之俱死。」

translations.literal: Yet my wife is ill; she cannot live on alone; I ask to die together with her."
translations.idiomatic: But my wife is ill and cannot survive alone; let us die together.

sentences.zh: 旻聞之，即並戮其妻於市，以其事白漢，以明無他。

translations.literal: When Min heard this, he immediately had his wife executed in the market as well, reported the matter to Han to show he had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Min had Xiang's sick wife killed in the marketplace too, then wrote the court to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 已而周太祖果代漢，降封赟湘陰公。

translations.literal: Before long Zhou Taizu did indeed supplant Han and demoted Yun to Duke of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guo replaced the Han dynasty and reduced Yun to Duke of Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 旻遣牙將李鋋奉書周太祖，求赟歸太原，而赟已死。

translations.literal: Min sent his military tooth Li Qian with a letter to Zhou Taizu asking that Yun be returned to Taiyuan, but Yun was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Min sent an aide, Li Qian, petitioning for Yun's return to Taiyuan—but Yun was already dead.

sentences.zh: 旻慟哭，為李驤立祠，歲時祠之。

translations.literal: Min wept bitterly, built a shrine to Li Xiang, and offered sacrifice to him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Min mourned bitterly, raised a shrine to Li Xiang, and sacrificed to him each year.

sentences.zh: 已而兀欲為述軋所弒，述律代立。

translations.literal: Before long Wuyu was assassinated by Shuzha, and Shulü succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Wuyu was murdered by Shuzha, and Shulü came to the throne.

sentences.zh: 旻遣樞密直學士王得中聘於述律，求兵以攻周。

translations.literal: Min sent Academician Wang Dezong on an embassy to Shulü seeking troops to attack Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Min sent Privy Council academician Wang Dezong to Shulü to request troops against Zhou.

sentences.zh: 述律遣蕭禹厥率兵五萬助旻。

translations.literal: Shulü sent Xiao Yuque at the head of fifty thousand men to assist Min.
translations.idiomatic: Shulü dispatched Xiao Yuque with fifty thousand men to aid him.

sentences.zh: 旻出陰地攻晉州，為王峻所敗。

translations.literal: Min advanced from Yin territory to attack Jin Prefecture and was defeated by Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Min raided from Yinzhou toward Jin Prefecture and was routed by Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 是歲大寒，旻軍凍餒，亡失過半。

translations.literal: That year the cold was extreme; Min's army suffered from cold and hunger, with more than half lost.
translations.idiomatic: That winter was savage; hunger and frost claimed more than half his force.

sentences.zh: 明年，又攻府州，為折德扆所敗，德扆因取岢嵐軍。

translations.literal: The next year he again attacked Fu Prefecture, was defeated by She Deyi; Deyi thereupon took Ke-lan Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked Fu Prefecture, lost to She Deyi, who then seized Ke-lan garrison.

sentences.zh: 周太祖崩，旻聞之喜，遣使乞兵於契丹。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu died; when Min heard it he rejoiced and sent envoys begging troops from Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei died Min rejoiced and asked the Khitans for troops.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣楊袞將鐵馬萬騎及奚諸部兵五六萬人號稱十萬以助旻。

translations.literal: The Khitans sent Yang Gun leading ten thousand iron cavalry and fifty or sixty thousand troops of the Xi and other tribes, claiming one hundred thousand, to aid Min.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan sent Yang Gun with ten thousand armored horse and fifty or sixty thousand Xi and allied riders—nominally a hundred thousand—to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 旻以張元徽為先鋒，自將騎兵三萬攻潞州。

translations.literal: Min made Zhang Yuanhui vanguard and personally led thirty thousand horsemen to attack Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He put Zhang Yuanhui in the van and led thirty thousand cavalry against Luzhou himself.

sentences.zh: 潞州李筠遣穆令鈞以步騎三千拒元徽於太平驛，元徽擊敗之，益圍潞州。

translations.literal: Li Yun of Luzhou sent Mu Lingjun with three thousand foot and horse to oppose Yuanhui at Taiping Station; Yuanhui routed him and pressed the siege of Luzhou tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou's Li Yun sent Mu Lingjun with three thousand mixed troops to meet Yuanhui at Taiping Post; Yuanhui smashed them and tightened the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 是時，世宗新即位，以謂旻幸周有大喪，而天子新立，必不能出兵，宜自將以擊其不意。

translations.literal: At this time Shizong had just taken the throne; he judged that Min, seeing Zhou in great mourning and a new Son of Heaven, would be unable to march out, and that he himself ought to take the field to strike where they would not expect it.
translations.idiomatic: The new Zhou emperor Chai Rong assumed Min would exploit the court's mourning and his own fresh accession—no army would come. He resolved to lead the campaign himself and surprise them.

sentences.zh: 自宰相馮道等多言不可，世宗意甚銳。

translations.literal: Feng Dao and other ministers mostly said it could not be done, yet Shizong's resolve was very firm.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao and others urged against it, but Shizong's mind was set.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年三月親征，甲午，戰於高平，李重進、白重贊將左，樊愛能、何徽將右，向訓、史彥超居中軍，張永德以禁兵衛蹕。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Xiande he led a personal expedition; on the jiawu day they fought at Gaoping. Li Chongjin and Bai Chongzan commanded the left, Fan Aineng and He Hui the right, Xiang Xun and Shi Yanchao the center, and Zhang Yongde guarded the imperial biao with the forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, Xiande 1: he marched in person. On jiawu day the armies met at Gaoping—Li Chongjin and Bai Chongzan on the left, Fan Aineng and He Hui on the right, Xiang Xun and Shi Yanchao in the center, Zhang Yongde shielding the imperial train with the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 旻亦列為三陣，張元徽居東偏，楊袞居西偏，旻居其中。

translations.literal: Min also drew up three lines: Zhang Yuanhui on the eastern wing, Yang Gun on the western, Min himself in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Min arrayed three corps—Yuanhui east, Yang Gun west, himself in the middle.

sentences.zh: 袞望周師謂旻曰：「敵也，未可輕動。」

translations.literal: Gun looked at the Zhou army and said to Min: "These are our foes—we must not move rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun studied the Zhou lines and warned, "That is a real enemy—do not strike lightly.

sentences.zh: 旻奮髯曰：「時不可失，無妄言也！」

translations.literal: Min bristled his beard and said: "The moment must not be lost—do not talk nonsense!"
translations.idiomatic: Min stroked his beard and snapped, "The hour will not wait—enough foolish talk!

sentences.zh: 衮怒而去。

translations.literal: Gun left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Gun stalked off in a rage.

sentences.zh: 旻號令東偏先進，王得中叩馬諫曰：「南風甚急，非北軍之利也，宜少待之。」

translations.literal: Min ordered the eastern wing to advance first; Wang Dezong seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated: "The south wind is very strong—not to the northern army's advantage; we ought to wait a little."
translations.idiomatic: Min ordered the eastern wing forward. Wang Dezong caught his bridle: "This fierce south wind favors the enemy—not us. Hold a while.

sentences.zh: 旻怒曰：「老措大，毋妄沮吾軍！」

translations.literal: Min raged: "Old bookworm—do not recklessly discourage my army!"
translations.idiomatic: Min snarled, "You old pedant—do not stammer at my host!

sentences.zh: 即麾元徽，元徽擊周右軍，兵始交，愛能、徽退走，其騎軍亂，步卒數千棄甲叛降元徽，呼萬歲聲振川谷。

translations.literal: He immediately waved Yuanhui forward; Yuanhui struck Zhou's right wing; as the ranks met, Aineng and Hui retreated; their cavalry fell into disorder; several thousand foot soldiers cast off armor and surrendered to Yuanhui, crying ten thousand years till the valleys rang.
translations.idiomatic: He waved Yuanhui on. Yuanhui charged the Zhou right; at first clash Fan Aineng and He Hui fled; cavalry broke; thousands of infantry threw down arms and surrendered to Yuanhui, shouting "Long live!" till valleys echoed.

sentences.zh: 世宗大駭，躬督戰士，士皆奮命爭先，而風勢愈盛，旻自麾赤幟收軍，軍不可遏，旻遂敗。

translations.literal: Shizong was greatly alarmed and personally urged the warriors on; the soldiers all strove to be first; the wind grew still stronger; Min himself waved red banners to recall the army, but the army could not be stopped; Min was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was shaken but rode the line himself; men fought desperately; the wind rose fiercer still; Min waved red flags to recall his host—the host would not heed—Min was beaten.

sentences.zh: 日暮，旻收余兵萬人阻澗而止。

translations.literal: At dusk Min gathered the remaining ten thousand men and blocked the streambed to halt.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he rallied ten thousand survivors and barred a ravine to stand.

sentences.zh: 是時，周之後軍，劉詞將之，在後未至，而世宗銳於速戰，戰已勝，詞軍繼至，因乘勝追擊之，旻又大敗，輜重器甲、乘輿服御物皆為周師所獲。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou's rear guard under Liu Ci had not yet arrived; Shizong was keen on a quick battle; once victory was won, Ci's army came up and pressed the pursuit; Min was again heavily defeated; baggage, armor, carriages, robes, and imperial regalia were all taken by Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ci's rearguard had not caught up; Shizong fought fast and won; then Ci arrived and pursued; Min suffered a second rout; wagons, armor, chariots, court dress, and imperial gear fell to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 旻獨乘契丹黃騮，自雕窠嶺間道馳去，夜失道山谷間，得村民為鄉導，誤趨平陽，得他道以歸，而張元徽戰歿於陣。

translations.literal: Min alone rode the Khitan yellow steed and fled by a path through Diaoke Ridge; at night he lost the way in the mountains; a villager guided him; he mistakenly hurried toward Pingyang; found another road and returned; Zhang Yuanhui fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Min alone fled on a yellow Khitan charger by mountain paths through Diaoke Ridge; night lost him in the hills until a farmer led him—wrongly toward Pingyang, then by another track home—while Yuanhui died on the field.

sentences.zh: 楊袞怒旻，按兵西偏不戰，故獨全軍而返。

translations.literal: Yang Gun was angry with Min; he held his western wing and did not fight, so his army alone returned intact.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gun, furious at Min, held the west wing idle and marched home whole.

sentences.zh: 旻歸，為黃騮治廄，飾以金銀，食以三品料，號「自在將軍」。

translations.literal: When Min returned he built a stable for the yellow steed, adorned it with gold and silver, fed it third-rank rations, and styled it "General at Ease."
translations.idiomatic: Back in Taiyuan he housed the horse in a gilded stable, fed it third-rank provender, and titled it "The Unfettered General."

sentences.zh: 世宗休軍潞州，大宴將士，斬敗將樊愛能、何徽等七十餘人，軍威大振。

translations.literal: Shizong rested the army at Luzhou and held a great feast for the commanders; he executed more than seventy defeated generals including Fan Aineng and He Hui; military awe was greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong paused at Luzhou, banqueted his captains, and beheaded seventy-odd failed commanders, Fan and He among them; discipline surged.

sentences.zh: 進攻太原，遣符彥卿、史彥超北控忻口，以斷契丹援路。

translations.literal: He pressed on toward Taiyuan, sent Fu Yanqing and Shi Yanchao north to hold Xin Ford and cut Khitan relief.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Taiyuan, posting Fu Yanqing and Shi Yanchao at Xin Ford to sever Khitan aid.

sentences.zh: 太原城方四十里，周師去城三百步，圍之匝，自四月至於六月，攻之不克，而彥卿等為契丹所敗，彥超戰歿，世宗遽班師。

translations.literal: Taiyuan's walls measured forty li; Zhou encamped three hundred paces out and wrapped the city round; from the fourth month to the sixth month they assaulted without success; Yanqing and the rest were beaten by Khitan; Yanchao died in battle; Shizong withdrew in haste.
translations.idiomatic: The forty-li walls defied them from April through June; Yanqing's force was routed by Khitan; Yanchao fell; Shizong hurried south.

sentences.zh: 初，周師圍城也，旻遣王得中送楊袞以歸，因乞援兵於契丹，契丹發數萬騎助旻，遣得中先還。

translations.literal: When Zhou first besieged the city, Min had Wang Dezong escort Yang Gun home while begging more Khitan troops; Khitan sent tens of thousands of horse to help Min and sent Dezong back ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the siege Min sent Dezong to escort Yang Gun home and plead for reinforcements; Khitan dispatched tens of thousands and sent Dezong ahead.

sentences.zh: 至代州，代州將桑珪殺防禦使鄭處謙，以城降周，並送得中於周。

translations.literal: Reaching Dai Prefecture, its general Sang Gui killed Defender Zheng Chuqian, surrendered the city to Zhou, and handed Dezong to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Dai, General Sang Gui slew the defender Zheng Chuqian, yielded the city to Zhou, and delivered Dezong.

sentences.zh: 世宗召問得中虜助兵多少，得中言送袞歸，無所求也，世宗信之。

translations.literal: Shizong summoned and questioned Dezong how many Khitan auxiliaries there were; Dezong said escorting Gun home involved no request; Shizong believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong questioned Dezong on Khitan numbers; Dezong claimed he had only escorted Gun back—no aid asked—and was believed.

sentences.zh: 已而契丹敗符彥卿於忻口，得中遂見殺。

translations.literal: Soon Khitan defeated Fu Yanqing at Xin Ford; Dezong was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan soon routed Fu Yanqing at Xin Ford; Dezong was executed.

sentences.zh: 旻自敗於高平，已而被圍，以憂得疾，明年十一月卒，年六十，子承鈞立。

translations.literal: After his defeat at Gaoping Min was besieged; grief brought illness; he died the next year in the eleventh month, aged sixty; his son Chengjun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Broken at Gaoping, then besieged, he sickened with care and died at sixty in the eleventh month of the following year; Chengjun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 承鈞，旻次子也。

translations.literal: Chengjun was Min's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun was Min's second son.

sentences.zh: 少頗好學，工書。

translations.literal: In youth he was quite studious and skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He had been studious as a youth and wrote a fine hand.

sentences.zh: 旻卒，承鈞遣人奉表契丹，自稱男。

translations.literal: When Min died, Chengjun sent a memorial to Khitan styling himself "your male child."
translations.idiomatic: On Min's death he sent Khitan a petition calling himself the emperor's "boy."

sentences.zh: 述律答之以詔，呼承鈞為兒，許其嗣位。

translations.literal: Shulü answered with an edict, addressing Chengjun as "son," and granted his succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shulü replied by edict, hailed him as "son," and confirmed his throne.

sentences.zh: 初，旻常謂張元徽等曰：「吾以高祖之業，赟之冤，義不為郭公屈爾，期與公等勉力以復家國之仇。

translations.literal: Formerly Min often told Zhang Yuanhui and others: "On account of Gaozu's enterprise and Yun's grievance, by right I cannot bow to Lord Guo; let us strive together to avenge our house and state.
translations.idiomatic: Min had told Yuanhui and others, "Gaozu's realm and Yun's blood forbid me to bend to Guo—we must regain our patrimony.

sentences.zh: 至於稱帝一方，豈獲已也，顧我是何天子，爾亦是何節度使？」

translations.literal: As for proclaiming myself emperor on one side, how could that be helped? Only consider what sort of Son of Heaven I am, and what sort of military governors you are?"
translations.idiomatic: Proclaiming myself emperor in one corner—was that my wish? Think what Son of Heaven I am, and what sort of governors you are!

sentences.zh: 故其僭號仍稱乾祐，不改元，不立宗廟，四時之祭，用家人禮。

translations.literal: Therefore his usurped title still used Qianyou; he did not change the era name; he did not establish an ancestral temple; the seasonal sacrifices used household ritual.
translations.idiomatic: So his throne still bore the era Qianyou; no new reign title; no imperial temple; sacrifices followed family rites.

sentences.zh: 承鈞既立，始赦境內，改乾祐十年曰天會元年，立七廟於顯聖宮。

translations.literal: Once Chengjun reigned he first amnestied the realm, changed the tenth year of Qianyou to the first year of Tianhui, and erected seven temples at Xiansheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun then declared amnesty, renamed Qianyou 10 as Tianhui 1, and raised seven shrines at Xiansheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣高勛助承鈞，承鈞遣李存瑰與勛攻上黨，無所得而還。

translations.literal: Khitan sent Gao Xun to aid Chengjun; Chengjun sent Li Cungui with Xun to attack Shangdang and returned empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan sent Gao Xun; Chengjun paired Li Cungui with him against Shangdang but gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 明年，世宗北伐契丹，下三關，契丹使來告急，承鈞將發兵，而世宗班師，乃已。

translations.literal: Next year Shizong campaigned north against Khitan, took three passes; Khitan sent urgent appeals; Chengjun was about to march out when Shizong withdrew and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Shizong marched on Khitan and seized three passes; urgent Khitan pleas moved Chengjun to mobilize—until Shizong retired and he stood down.

sentences.zh: 宋興，昭義節度使李筠叛命，遣其將劉繼沖、判官孫孚奉表稱臣，執其監軍周光遜、李廷玉送於太原，乞兵為援。

translations.literal: When Song rose, Zhaoyi governor Li Yun rebelled; he sent Liu Jichong and aide Sun Fu with a memorial of submission, handed his overseers Zhou Guangxun and Li Tingyu to Taiyuan, begging troops.
translations.idiomatic: As Song began, Li Yun of Zhaoyi rebelled, sent Liu Jichong and Sun Fu to swear fealty, and delivered overseers Zhou Guangxun and Li Tingyu to Taiyuan for aid.

sentences.zh: 承鈞欲謀於契丹，繼沖道筠意，請無用契丹兵。

translations.literal: Chengjun wished to consult Khitan; Jichong relayed Yun's wish to employ no Khitan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun meant to call on Khitan; Jichong conveyed Yun's plea to keep Khitan out.

sentences.zh: 承鈞即率其國兵自將出團柏谷，群臣餞之汾水。

translations.literal: Chengjun thereupon led his native troops in person through Tuanbai Valley; the ministers saw him off at the Fen River.
translations.idiomatic: He led his own army through Tuanbai Gorge while ministers toasted him on the Fen.

sentences.zh: 僕射趙華曰：「李筠舉事輕易，陛下不圖成敗，空國興師，臣實憂之。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhao Hua said: "Li Yun's uprising is rash; Your Majesty marches without weighing success—emptying the state—and I am deeply troubled."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hua warned, "Yun acts rashly; you risk the realm without judging the odds—I fear disaster.

sentences.zh: 承鈞至太平驛，封筠隴西郡王。

translations.literal: At Taiping Post Chengjun enfeoffed Yun as Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiping Post he created Yun Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 筠見承鈞儀衛不備，非如王者，悔臣之，筠因自陳受周氏恩，不忍背德。

translations.literal: Yun saw Chengjun's escort unfit for a king, regretted his submission, and confessed the Zhou had shown him kindness he could not betray.
translations.idiomatic: Yun found Chengjun's train unkingly, repented his oath, and admitted Zhou's kindness left him unable to rebel.

sentences.zh: 而承鈞與周世仇也，聞筠言亦不悅。

translations.literal: But Chengjun bore Zhou an inherited feud; hearing Yun he was displeased too.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun, Zhou's hereditary foe, took equal offense.

sentences.zh: 遣宣徽使盧贊監其軍，筠心益不平，與贊多不葉，承鈞遣宰相衛融和解之。

translations.literal: He sent Commissioner Lu Zan to oversee Yun's army; Yun grew more resentful and clashed with Zan; Chengjun sent Chancellor Wei Rong to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Lu Zan as supervisor; friction grew; Wei Rong was sent to patch peace.

sentences.zh: 已而筠敗死，衛融被執至京師，太祖皇帝問融承鈞所以助筠反狀，融言不遜，太祖命以鐵楇擊其首，流血被面，融呼曰：「臣得死所矣！」

translations.literal: When Yun was defeated and killed, Wei Rong was seized and brought to the capital; Taizu asked what aid Chengjun had given Yun; Rong answered insolently; Taizu had an iron pestle strike his head until blood bathed his face; Rong cried: "I have found the place to die!"
translations.idiomatic: Yun fell; Wei Rong was captured; Song's Taizu asked how Chengjun helped the revolt; Rong answered rudely; an iron maul split his brow; he shouted, "A worthy death!

sentences.zh: 太祖顧左右曰：「此忠臣也。」

translations.literal: Taizu looked to his attendants and said: "This is a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told his men, "Here is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 釋之，命以良藥傅其瘡。

translations.literal: He released him and ordered good medicine applied to his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He freed him and sent salves.

sentences.zh: 遣融致書於承鈞，求周光遜等，約亦歸融太原。

translations.literal: He sent Rong with a letter to Chengjun demanding Zhou Guangxun and others, promising Rong's return to Taiyuan as well.
translations.idiomatic: Rong carried a letter seeking Zhou Guangxun and company, offering to send Rong back too.

sentences.zh: 承鈞不報，融遂留京師。

translations.literal: Chengjun did not reply; Rong stayed at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun did not answer; Rong remained.

sentences.zh: 承鈞謂趙華曰：「不聽公言，幾至於敗。

translations.literal: Chengjun said to Zhao Hua: "Had I listened to you, I would nearly have failed.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhao Hua, "Your counsel almost saved me—

sentences.zh: 然失衛融、盧贊，吾以為恨爾。」

translations.literal: Yet losing Wei Rong and Lu Zan—I regret it."
translations.idiomatic: but losing Rong and Zan grieves me."

sentences.zh: 承鈞由此益重儒者，以抱腹山人郭無為參議國政。

translations.literal: From this Chengjun valued scholars all the more and made the recluse Guo Youwei a participant in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he prized scholars and installed the mountain man Guo Youwei in counsel.

sentences.zh: 無為，棣州人，方顙鳥喙，好學多聞，善談辯。

translations.literal: Youwei was from Di Prefecture, with a broad forehead and beaklike nose, fond of study and widely informed, skilled at disputation.
translations.idiomatic: A Di Prefecture man with high brow and hooked nose, widely read and silver-tongued.

sentences.zh: 嘗衣褐為道士，居武當山。

translations.literal: He had worn brown robes as a Daoist priest on Mount Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: He had lived as a Daoist in brown on Wudang.

sentences.zh: 周太祖討李守貞於河中，無為詣軍門上謁，詢以當世之務，太祖奇之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu besieged Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Youwei came to the camp gate and was questioned on current affairs; the Taizu thought him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: During Guo's siege of Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Youwei appeared at camp and debated policy; Guo was impressed.

sentences.zh: 或謂太祖曰：「公為漢大臣，握重兵居外，而延縱橫之士，非所以防微慮遠之道也。」

translations.literal: Someone told the Taizu: "You are a Han minister holding great armies abroad while entertaining roaming strategists—not the way to guard against small beginnings and plan far ahead."
translations.idiomatic: An aide warned, "A Han minister with armies abroad who hosts roaming strategists invites suspicion.

sentences.zh: 由是太祖不納。

translations.literal: The Taizu therefore did not take him in.
translations.idiomatic: Guo declined him.

sentences.zh: 無為去，隱抱腹山。

translations.literal: Youwei left and hid on Mount Baofu.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei retired to Mount Baofu.

sentences.zh: 承鈞內樞密使段常識之，薦其材，承鈞以諫議大夫召之，遂以為相。

translations.literal: Interior Commissioner Duan Chang knew him and recommended his talent; Chengjun summoned him as Remonstrance Officer and then made him chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang of the privy council praised him; Chengjun made him Remonstrance Officer, then chancellor.

sentences.zh: 五年，宿衛殿直行首王隱、劉紹、趙鸞等謀作亂，事覺被誅，其詞連段常，乃罷常樞密為汾州刺史，縊殺之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, palace guards Wang Yin, Liu Shao, Zhao Luan and others plotted rebellion; exposed, they were executed; their testimony implicated Duan Chang; Chang was removed from the privy council to prefect of Fen and strangled.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year: guards Wang Yin, Liu Shao, Zhao Luan plotted treason, were killed, and implicated Chang—demoted to Fen prefect and strangled.

sentences.zh: 自旻世凡舉事必稟契丹，而承鈞之立多略。

translations.literal: From Min's time every campaign had been reported to Khitan; Chengjun's accession was mostly kept from them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Min every move was cleared with Khitan; Chengjun often acted without telling them.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣使者責承鈞改元、援李筠、殺段常不以告，承鈞惶恐謝罪。

translations.literal: Khitan sent envoys rebuking Chengjun for changing the era, aiding Li Yun, and killing Duan Chang without notice; Chengjun bowed in fear and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys rebuked his new era, aid to Yun, and Chang's death unreported; he prostrated himself in apology.

sentences.zh: 使者至契丹輒見留，承鈞奉之愈謹，而契丹待承鈞益薄。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys reached Khitan they were detained; Chengjun treated them with ever greater deference, while Khitan treated Chengjun ever more coldly.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys to Khitan were routinely held hostage; Chengjun grew more obsequious, Khitan more dismissive.

sentences.zh: 承鈞自李筠敗而失契丹之援，無復南侵之意。

translations.literal: After Li Yun's defeat Chengjun lost Khitan support and had no further thought of invading south.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun's defeat Chengjun lost Khitan backing and abandoned any plan to strike south.

sentences.zh: 地狹產薄，以歲輸契丹，故國用日削，乃拜五臺山僧繼颙為鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: The land was narrow and yields thin; yearly tribute went to Khitan, so state revenues daily shrank; he therefore appointed the Mount Wutai monk Jiyong as Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Territory was cramped and poor; annual Khitan tribute drained the treasury, so he named the Wutai monk Jiyong Director of Guests.

sentences.zh: 繼颙，故燕王劉守光之子，守光之死，以孽子得不殺，削髮為浮圖，後居五臺山，為人多智，善商財利，自旻世頗以賴之。

translations.literal: Jiyong was son of the former Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang; at Shouguang's death, as an illegitimate son he was spared, shaved his head and became a monk, later dwelt on Mount Wutai; he was clever and skilled at commerce and profit; from Min's time the house relied on him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyong, illegitimate son of Liu Shouguang of Yan, survived his father's fall by taking vows and settling on Wutai—a shrewd trader the Liu house had leaned on since Min's day.

sentences.zh: 繼颙能講《華嚴經》，四方供施，多積畜以佐國用。

translations.literal: Jiyong could expound the 《Avatamsaka Sutra》; offerings came from all quarters; he amassed much to supplement state funds.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on the 《Avatamsaka》, drew donations from every direction, and stockpiled wealth for the state.

sentences.zh: 五臺當契丹界上，繼颙常得其馬以獻，號「添都馬」，歲率數百匹。

translations.literal: Wutai lay on the Khitan border; Jiyong often obtained their horses to present, styled "Supplementary Metropolitan Horses," several hundred each year.
translations.idiomatic: Wutai bordered Khitan; he procured their horses as tribute—"Supplementary Capital Horses"—hundreds yearly.

sentences.zh: 又於柏谷置銀冶，募民鑿山取礦，烹銀以輸，劉氏仰以足用，即其冶建寶興軍。

translations.literal: He also set up a silver smeltery at Bai Valley, recruited people to mine the mountains, smelted silver for delivery; the Liu house relied on this for sufficiency and at the smeltery established Baoxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: At Bai Valley he opened silver works, hired miners, and smelted tribute silver that kept the Liu treasury solvent—founding Baoxing garrison at the site.

sentences.zh: 繼颙後累官至太師、中書令，以老病卒，追封定王。

translations.literal: Jiyong later rose through offices to Grand Preceptor and Grand Secretary; he died of old age and illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Preceptor and Grand Secretary, died in old age, and was posthumously made Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝嘗因界上諜者謂承鈞曰：「君家與周氏為世仇，宜其不屈，今我與爾無所間，何為困此一方之人也？

translations.literal: Taizu once sent word through a border spy to Chengjun: "Your house and the Zhou are hereditary foes—it is fitting you do not submit; yet between you and me there is no quarrel—why afflict the people of this corner?
translations.idiomatic: Song's Taizu once told a border agent to ask Chengjun, "Your house and Zhou are ancient enemies—no wonder you resist; but I bear you no grudge—why make this pocket of land suffer?

sentences.zh: 若有志於中國，宜下太行以決勝負。」

translations.literal: If you have ambition toward the Central States, you ought to descend the Taihang and settle victory or defeat."
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to contest the empire, come down through the Taihang and fight it out.

sentences.zh: 承鈞遣諜者復命曰：「河東土地兵甲，不足以當中國之十一；

translations.literal: Chengjun sent the spy back with the reply: "Hedong's territory and arms are not one-tenth of the Central States;
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun sent back word: "Hedong's land and arms are less than a tenth of yours—

sentences.zh: 然承鈞家世非叛者，區區守此，蓋懼漢氏之不血食也。」

translations.literal: yet Chengjun's house from of old is not rebellious; holding this little corner, I fear only that the Han line will lack sacrificial offerings."
translations.idiomatic: yet my line was never rebel-born; I hold this corner lest the Han house lose its sacrifices forever.

sentences.zh: 太祖哀其言，笑謂諜者曰：「為我語承鈞，開爾一路以為生。」

translations.literal: Taizu pitied his words and, smiling, told the spy: "Tell Chengjun for me: I will open you a path to live."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was moved, smiled, and said, "Tell him I will leave him a road to live by.

sentences.zh: 故終其世不加兵。

translations.literal: Therefore to the end of his life he did not send troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: So for Chengjun's lifetime Song never marched against him.

sentences.zh: 承鈞立十三年病卒，其養子繼恩立。

translations.literal: Chengjun reigned thirteen years and died of illness; his adopted son Jien succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After thirteen years Chengjun died; his adopted heir Jien took the throne.

sentences.zh: 繼恩本姓薛氏，父釗為卒，旻以女妻之，生繼恩。

translations.literal: Jien was originally surnamed Xue; his father Zhao was a soldier; Min gave him his daughter in marriage and Jien was born.
translations.idiomatic: Jien was born Xue; his father Zhao was a common soldier whom Min married to a daughter—thus Jien.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖以釗婿也，除其軍籍，置之門下。

translations.literal: Gaozu of Han, because Zhao was his son-in-law, removed him from the military rolls and kept him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, as Zhao was family, struck him from the rolls and kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 釗無材能，高祖衣食之而無所用。

translations.literal: Zhao had no talent; Gaozu fed and clothed him but found no use for him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had no ability; Gaozu clothed and fed him but never employed him.

sentences.zh: 妻以旻女常居中，釗罕得見，釗常怏怏，因醉拔佩刀刺之，傷而不死，釗即自裁。

translations.literal: His wife, Min's daughter, always stayed in the inner quarters; Zhao rarely saw her; Zhao was often discontent; once drunk he drew his sword and stabbed her; she was wounded but did not die; Zhao then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Min's daughter kept to the inner quarters; Zhao seldom saw her, grew bitter, and once, drunk, stabbed her—she lived—and then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 旻女後適何氏，生子繼元，而何氏及旻女皆卒。

translations.literal: Min's daughter later married the He family and bore Jiyuan; both the He family and Min's daughter died.
translations.idiomatic: She later wed a He and bore Jiyuan; both she and the He clan died.

sentences.zh: 旻以其子承鈞無子，乃以二子命承鈞養為子。

translations.literal: Because his son Chengjun had no sons, Min ordered the two boys adopted as Chengjun's sons.
translations.idiomatic: As Chengjun had no heir, Min had both boys adopted as his sons.

sentences.zh: 承鈞立，以繼恩為太原尹。

translations.literal: When Chengjun reigned he made Jien governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Chengjun made Jien prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 承鈞嘗謂郭無為曰：「繼恩純孝，然非濟世之才，恐不能了我家事。」

translations.literal: Chengjun once told Guo Youwei: "Jien is purely filial, yet lacks talent to save the age—I fear he cannot finish my family's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun once told Guo Youwei, "Jien is dutiful but no statesman—I doubt he can settle our house's affairs.

sentences.zh: 無為不對。

translations.literal: Youwei did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei said nothing.

sentences.zh: 承鈞病臥勤政閣，召無為，執手以後事付之。

translations.literal: Chengjun lay ill in the Diligence-in-Government Pavilion, summoned Youwei, took his hand and entrusted him with later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dying in the Diligence Pavilion, he summoned Youwei, clasped his hand, and entrusted the aftermath.

sentences.zh: 承鈞卒，繼恩告哀於契丹而後立。

translations.literal: When Chengjun died, Jien announced mourning to Khitan and only then took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengjun's death Jien notified Khitan of mourning, then enthroned himself.

sentences.zh: 繼恩服缞裳視事，寢處皆居勤政閣，而承鈞故執事百司宿衛者皆在太原府廨。

translations.literal: Jien wore mourning hemp and handled affairs; he slept and dwelt entirely in the Diligence Pavilion, while Chengjun's former administrators, the hundred offices, and the guards all remained in the Taiyuan government compound.
translations.idiomatic: Jien governed in hemp mourning and lived only in the Diligence Pavilion; Chengjun's old officials and guards stayed in the prefectural offices.

sentences.zh: 九月，繼恩置酒會諸大臣宗子，飲罷，臥閣中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jien set out wine and feasted the ministers and clansmen; when the drinking ended he lay down in the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he banqueted ministers and kin, then retired to the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 供奉官侯霸榮率十餘人挺刃入閣，閉戶而殺之。

translations.literal: Palace supply officer Hou Barong led more than ten men with drawn blades into the pavilion, shut the door, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officer Hou Barong and a dozen men burst in, barred the door, and slew him.

sentences.zh: 郭無為遣人以梯登屋入，殺霸榮並其黨。

translations.literal: Guo Youwei sent men up ladders onto the roof to enter and killed Barong and his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Youwei sent men over the roof and killed Barong and his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 初，承鈞之語郭無為也，繼恩怨無為不助己，及立，欲逐之而未果，故霸榮之亂，人皆以謂無為之謀，霸榮死，口滅而無知者。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Chengjun's words to Guo Youwei, Jien resented Youwei for not supporting him; once enthroned he wished to drive him out but did not succeed; therefore in Barong's turmoil people all said it was Youwei's plot; when Barong died the mouth was silenced and none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Jien had resented Youwei since Chengjun's remark that he lacked talent; on taking power he tried to oust him and failed—so when Barong struck, rumor blamed Youwei; Barong's death left no witness.

sentences.zh: 無為迎繼元而立之。

translations.literal: Youwei welcomed Jiyuan and enthroned him.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei installed Jiyuan as ruler.

sentences.zh: 繼元為人忍。

translations.literal: Jiyuan was a man of cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan was ruthless by nature.

sentences.zh: 旻子十餘人，皆無可稱者。

translations.literal: Min had more than ten sons, none worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Min had a dozen sons, none distinguished.

sentences.zh: 當繼元時，有鎬、鍇、锜、錫、銑，於繼元為諸父，皆為繼元所殺，獨銑以佯愚獲免。

translations.literal: In Jiyuan's time there were Gao, Kai, Qi, Xi, and Xian—uncles to Jiyuan—all killed by Jiyuan; only Xian escaped by feigning stupidity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiyuan his uncles Gao, Kai, Qi, Xi, and Xian were all killed—only Xian survived by playing the fool.

sentences.zh: 承鈞妻郭氏，繼元兄弟自少母之。

translations.literal: Chengjun's wife was of the Guo clan; Jiyuan and his brothers had from youth treated her as mother.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjun's consort was a Guo; Jiyuan and his brothers had called her mother since childhood.

sentences.zh: 繼元妻段氏，嘗以小過為郭氏所責，既而以它疾而卒，繼元疑其殺之。

translations.literal: Jiyuan's wife was of the Duan clan; once rebuked by the Guo for a small fault, she later died of another illness; Jiyuan suspected the Guo had killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan's wife Duan had once been scolded by Lady Guo for a trifle; she later died of illness—Jiyuan suspected murder.

sentences.zh: 及立，遣嬖者範超圖殺郭氏，郭氏方缞服哭承鈞於柩前，超執而縊殺之，於是劉氏之子孫無遺類矣。

translations.literal: Once enthroned he sent his favorite Fan Chao to plot killing the Guo; the Guo was in hemp mourning weeping for Chengjun before the coffin; Chao seized and strangled her—thus no descendant of the Liu house remained.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he sent his favorite Fan Chao to kill Lady Guo as she mourned before Chengjun's bier—strangling her—and with that the Liu line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 繼元立，改元曰廣運。

translations.literal: When Jiyuan reigned he changed the era name to Guangyun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan took the throne and proclaimed the era Guangyun.

sentences.zh: 王師北征，繼元閉城拒守，太祖皇帝以詔書招繼元出降，許以平盧軍節度使，郭無為安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: The imperial army marched north; Jiyuan shut the city and held out; Taizu sent an edict summoning Jiyuan to surrender, promising him military governor of Pinglu and Guo Youwei military governor of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Song's northern expedition found Jiyuan behind closed walls; Taizu offered surrender—Jiyuan as governor of Pinglu, Youwei of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 無為捧詔色動，而並人及繼元左右皆欲堅守以拒命。

translations.literal: Youwei, holding the edict, showed emotion on his face, but the people of Bing and those around Jiyuan all wished to hold firm and refuse the command.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei, reading the edict, wavered—but Bingzhou and Jiyuan's court wanted to hold out.

sentences.zh: 無為仰天慟哭，拔佩刀欲自裁，為左右所持。

translations.literal: Youwei looked to heaven and wept bitterly, drew his sword intending suicide, and was seized by those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Youwei wept to heaven and tried to fall on his sword; attendants restrained him.

sentences.zh: 繼元自下執其手，延之上坐，無為曰：「奈何以孤城拒百萬之王師？」

translations.literal: Jiyuan came down and took his hand, led him to the upper seat; Youwei said: "How can one lone city resist a million imperial troops?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiyuan came down, took his hand, and seated him above, while Youwei asked, "How can a lone city defy a million imperial troops?

sentences.zh: 蓋欲搖動並人，而並人守意益堅。

translations.literal: He wished to shake the resolve of the Bing people, but the Bing people's will to hold out grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to sway Bingzhou—but their will to resist only hardened.

sentences.zh: 宦者衛德貴察無為有異志，以告繼元，繼元遣人縊殺之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wei Degui perceived Youwei's contrary intent and reported to Jiyuan; Jiyuan sent men to strangle him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Wei Degui detected his disloyalty and told Jiyuan, who had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖皇帝命引汾水浸其城，水自城門入，而有積草自城中飄出塞之。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu had ordered the Fen River diverted to flood the city; water entered through the gate, but piled grass floated out from within and blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had the Fen diverted to flood Taiyuan; water poured through the gates until grass bundles floated out from within and choked the breach.

sentences.zh: 是時，王師頓兵甘草地中，會歲暑雨，軍士多疾，乃班師。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army encamped in Licorice Ground; it happened to be summer heat and rain; many soldiers fell ill, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped at Licorice Ground; summer heat and rain sickened the troops, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王師已去，繼元決城下水註之臺駘澤，水已落而城多摧圮。

translations.literal: After the imperial army had gone, Jiyuan breached the water within the city and channeled it to Taitai Marsh; when the water receded much of the wall was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: After Song withdrew, Jiyuan drained the flood into Taitai Marsh; as waters fell, much of the wall collapsed.

sentences.zh: 契丹使者韓知璠時在太原，嘆曰：「王師之引水浸城也，知其一而不知其二，若先浸而後涸，則並人無類矣！」

translations.literal: The Khitan envoy Han Zhifan was then in Taiyuan and sighed: "In flooding the city the imperial army knew one thing but not the second—if they had soaked it first and only then let it dry, none of the Bing people would remain!"
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoy Han Zhifan, present in Taiyuan, sighed, "Song knew half the trick of flooding—had they soaked the city and then let it dry, Bingzhou would have been annihilated!"

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，王師復北征，繼元窮窘，而並人猶欲堅守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo the imperial army again marched north; Jiyuan was desperate, yet the Bing people still wished to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 4 brought another northern campaign; Jiyuan was cornered, yet Bingzhou still wanted to resist.

sentences.zh: 其樞密副使馬峰老疾居於家，舁入見繼元，流涕以興亡諭之，繼元乃降。

translations.literal: His Vice Director of the Privy Council Ma Feng, old and ill, dwelt at home; he was carried in to see Jiyuan, wept, and admonished him with rise and fall; Jiyuan then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Vice privy councilor Ma Feng, aged and ill at home, was carried in weeping to lecture Jiyuan on survival—whereupon he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝御城北高臺受降，以繼元為右衛上將軍，封彭城公。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong took the high terrace north of the city to receive the surrender, made Jiyuan General of the Right Guard, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong received surrender on the north terrace, made him General of the Right Guard, and created him Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 其後事具國史。

translations.literal: His later affairs are fully recorded in the national history.
translations.idiomatic: His later career is recorded in the dynastic histories.

sentences.zh: 〈（旻年世興滅，諸書皆同，自周廣順元年建號，至皇朝太平興國四年滅，凡二十八年，余具年譜註。）〉

translations.literal: (The chronology of Min's rise and fall agrees in all books: from establishing his reign in the first year of Zhou Guangshun to destruction in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo of our dynasty—twenty-eight years in all; I have set out the year-by-year record in notes.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (All sources agree on Min's dates: he founded his state in Zhou Guangshun 1 and fell in our Taiping Xingguo 4—twenty-eight years; see my chronological notes.)〉
